title: Prakrama 1, Sarga 2. Narada's Sorrow
html:
Jagannatha Mishra and Shachi; the birth of Vishvarupa; Damodara Pandita's question; Narada sees the earth gripped by Kali

Verse 1

अथ तस्य गुरुश्चक्रे सर्वशास्त्रार्थवेदिनः।
पदवीमिति तत्त्वज्ञः श्रीमन्मिश्रपुरन्दरः॥१॥

atha tasya guruścakre sarvaśāstrārthavedinaḥ|
padavīmiti tattvajñaḥ śrīmanmiśrapurandaraḥ||1||

atha — then; tasya — to him; guruh — the guru; chakre — gave; sarva-shastra-artha-vedinah — who knew the meaning of all scriptures; padavim — the title; iti — thus; tattva-jnah — knowing the truth; shriman-mishra-purandarah — "Shriman Mishra Purandara".

1Then his guru, a knower of the truth, honoured him, who had mastered the meaning of all the scriptures, with the title "Shriman Mishra Purandara"1.

Verse 2

तमेकदा सत्कुलीनं पण्डितं धर्मिणां वरम्।
श्रीमन्नीलाम्बरो नाम चक्रवर्ती महामनाः॥२॥

tamekadā satkulīnaṁ paṇḍitaṁ dharmiṇāṁ varam|
śrīmannīlāmbaro nāma cakravartī mahāmanāḥ||2||

tam — him; ekada — once; sat-kulinam — of noble family; panditam — the learned man; dharminam — of the righteous; varam — the best; shriman — the illustrious; nilambarah — Nilambara; nama — by name; chakravarti — Chakravarti; maha-manah — great-minded.

2One day the illustrious and great-hearted Chakravarti named Nilambara summoned this learned man of noble family, the best of the righteous,

Verse 3

समाहूयाददत् कन्यां शचीं स कुलकृच्छदः।
तां प्राप्य सोऽपि ववृधे शचीमिव पुरन्दरः॥३॥

samāhūyādadat kanyāṁ śacīṁ sa kulakṛcchadaḥ|
tāṁ prāpya so'pi vavṛdhe śacīmiva purandaraḥ||3||

samahuya — having summoned; adadat — gave; kanyam — his daughter; shachim — Shachi; sah — he; kula-krich-chhadah — (unclear; perhaps "the support of his line"); tam — her; prapya — having obtained; sah api — he too; vavridhe — prospered; shachim — Shachi; iva — as; purandarah — Purandara (Indra).

3and he, the support of his line2, gave him his daughter Shachi in marriage. Having won her, Mishra prospered, like Purandara who won Shachi3.

Verse 4

ततो गेहे निवसतस्तस्य धर्मो व्यवर्धत।
आतिथ्यैः शान्तिकैः शौचैर्नित्यकाम्यक्रियाफलैः॥४॥

tato gehe nivasatastasya dharmo vyavardhata|
ātithyaiḥ śāntikaiḥ śaucairnityakāmyakriyāphalaiḥ||4||

tatah — then; gehe — at home; nivasatah — living; tasya — his; dharmah — dharma; vyavardhata — grew; atithyaih — by hospitality; shantikaih — by propitiatory rites; shauchaih — by purifications; nitya-kamya-kriya-phalaih — by the fruits of regular and optional rites.

4He lived at home, and his dharma kept growing — through hospitality, propitiatory rites, purifications, and the fruits of rites both regular and performed for a desired end.

Verse 5

तत्र कालेन कियता तस्याष्टौ कन्यकाः शुभाः।
बभूवुः क्रमशो दैवात्ताः पञ्चत्वं गताः शची॥५॥

tatra kālena kiyatā tasyāṣṭau kanyakāḥ śubhāḥ|
babhūvuḥ kramaśo daivāttāḥ pañcatvaṁ gatāḥ śacī||5||

tatra — there; kalena kiyata — in some time; tasya — to him; ashtau — eight; kanyakah — daughters; shubhah — lovely; babhuvuh — were born; kramashah — one after another; daivat — by fate; tah — they; panchatvam — death (lit. "return to the five elements"); gatah — met; shachi — Shachi (subject of v. 6).

5In the course of time eight lovely daughters were born to him one after another, but by the will of fate they all died. And Shachi,

Verse 6

वात्सल्यदुःखतप्तेन जगाम मनसा हरिम्।
पुत्रार्थं शरणं श्रीमान् पितृयज्ञं चकार सः॥६॥

vātsalyaduḥkhataptena jagāma manasā harim|
putrārthaṁ śaraṇaṁ śrīmān pitṛyajñaṁ cakāra saḥ||6||

vatsalya-duhkha-taptena — burnt by the grief of a mother's love; jagama — went; manasa — in mind; harim — to Hari; putra-artham — for a son; sharanam — for refuge; shriman — the illustrious; pitri-yajnam — sacrifice to the ancestors; chakara — performed; sah — he.

6her heart scorched by a mother's grief, took refuge in Hari within her mind, praying for a son; and the illustrious Mishra performed a sacrifice to the ancestors.

Verse 7

कालेन कियता लेभे पुत्रं सुरसुतोपमम्।
मुदमाप जगन्नाथो निधिं प्राप्य यथाधनः॥७॥

kālena kiyatā lebhe putraṁ surasutopamam|
mudamāpa jagannātho nidhiṁ prāpya yathādhanaḥ||7||

kalena kiyata — in some time; lebhe — obtained; putram — a son; sura-suta-upamam — like a son of the gods; mudam — joy; apa — attained; jagannathah — Jagannatha; nidhim — a treasure; prapya — finding; yatha — as; adhanah — a poor man.

7After some time he obtained a son like a son of the gods, and Jagannatha rejoiced like a poor man who has found a treasure.

Verse 8

नाम तस्य पिता चक्रे श्रीमतो विश्वरूपकः।
पठता तेन कालेन स्वल्पेनैव महात्मना॥८॥

nāma tasya pitā cakre śrīmato viśvarūpakaḥ|
paṭhatā tena kālena svalpenaiva mahātmanā||8||

nama — the name; tasya — to him; pita — the father; chakre — gave; shrimatah — the illustrious; vishvarupakah — "Vishvarupa"; pathata — studying; tena — by him; kalena — in a time; svalpena eva — very short; maha-atmana — by the great soul.

8The father named the illustrious boy Vishvarupa. In a very short time that great soul learned

Verse 9

वेदांश्च न्यायशास्त्रं च ज्ञातः सद्योग उत्तमः।
स सर्वज्ञः सुधीः शान्तः सर्वेषामुपकारकः॥९॥

vedāṁśca nyāyaśāstraṁ ca jñātaḥ sadyoga uttamaḥ|
sa sarvajñaḥ sudhīḥ śāntaḥ sarveṣāmupakārakaḥ||9||

vedan — the Vedas; cha — and; nyaya-shastram — the science of logic; cha — and; jnatah — became known; sad-yogah — endowed with true yoga; uttamah — excellent; sah — he; sarva-jnah — all-knowing; sudhih — wise; shantah — peaceful; sarvesham — to all; upakarakah — a benefactor.

9the Vedas and the science of logic and became renowned: excellent, endowed with true yoga, he was all-knowing, wise, serene, and a benefactor to all.

Verse 10

हरेर्ध्यानपरो नित्यं विषये नाकरोन्मनः।
श्रीमद्भागवतरसास्वादमत्तो निरन्तरम्॥१०॥

harerdhyānaparo nityaṁ viṣaye nākaronmanaḥ|
śrīmadbhāgavatarasāsvādamatto nirantaram||10||

hareh — of Hari; dhyana-parah — intent on meditation; nityam — always; vishaye — to sense objects; na — not; akarot — turned; manah — his mind; shrimad-bhagavata-rasa-asvada-mattah — intoxicated with tasting the rasa of the Srimad-Bhagavatam; nirantaram — ceaselessly.

10Ever absorbed in meditation on Hari, he never turned his mind to the things of the senses, and was ceaselessly intoxicated with the taste of the rasa of the Srimad-Bhagavatam.

Verse 11

तस्यानुजो जगद्योनिरजो जज्ञे स्वयं प्रभुः।
इन्द्रानुजो यथोपेन्द्रः कश्यपाददितेः सुतः॥११॥

tasyānujo jagadyonirajo jajñe svayaṁ prabhuḥ|
indrānujo yathopendraḥ kaśyapādaditeḥ sutaḥ||11||

tasya — his; anujah — younger brother; jagat-yonih — the source of the world; ajah — the unborn; jajne — was born; svayam — himself; prabhuh — the Lord; indra-anujah — Indra's younger brother; yatha — as; upendrah — Upendra; kashyapat — from Kashyapa; aditeh — from Aditi; sutah — the son.

11As his younger brother the Lord Himself was born, the unborn source of the world — just as Upendra, the younger brother of Indra, was born the son of Kashyapa and Aditi4.

Verse 12

हरिसङ्कीर्तनपरां कृत्वा त्रिजगतीं स्वयम्।
उषित्वा क्षेत्रप्रवरे पुरुषोत्तमसंज्ञके॥१२॥

harisaṅkīrtanaparāṁ kṛtvā trijagatīṁ svayam|
uṣitvā kṣetrapravare puruṣottamasaṁjñake||12||

hari-sankirtana-param — devoted to the sankirtana of Hari; kritva — having made; tri-jagatim — the three worlds; svayam — himself; ushitva — having lived; kshetra-pravare — in the foremost holy place; purushottama-samjnake — called Purushottama.

12He Himself made the three worlds devoted to the sankirtana of Hari. He dwelt in the foremost of holy places, called Purushottama;

Verse 13

कृत्वा भक्तिं हरौ शिक्षां कारयित्वा जनस्य सः।
श्रीवृन्दावनमाधुर्यमास्वाद्यास्वादयन् जनान्॥१३॥

kṛtvā bhaktiṁ harau śikṣāṁ kārayitvā janasya saḥ|
śrīvṛndāvanamādhuryamāsvādyāsvādayan janān||13||

kritva — having practised; bhaktim — devotion; harau — to Hari; shiksham — the teaching; karayitva — having caused to learn; janasya — the people; sah — he; shri-vrindavana-madhuryam — the sweetness of Sri Vrindavana; asvadya — having tasted; asvadayan — making taste; janan — the people.

13He showed devotion to Hari and taught it to the people; He tasted the sweetness of Sri Vrindavana and gave the people to taste it;

Verse 14

तारयित्वा जगत्कृत्स्नं वैकुण्ठस्थैः प्रसाधितः।
जगाम निलयं हृष्टो निजमेव महर्द्धिमत्॥१४॥

tārayitvā jagatkṛtsnaṁ vaikuṇṭhasthaiḥ prasādhitaḥ|
jagāma nilayaṁ hṛṣṭo nijameva maharddhimat||14||

tarayitva — having delivered; jagat — the world; kritsnam — entire; vaikuntha-sthaih — by the dwellers of Vaikuntha; prasadhitah — adorned (honoured); jagama — went; nilayam — to the abode; hrishtah — joyful; nijam eva — his very own; maharddhimat — full of great splendour.

14and, having delivered the whole world, honoured by the dwellers of Vaikuntha, He joyfully departed for His very own abode, rich in great splendour.

Verse 15

एतच्छ्रुत्वाद्भुतं प्राह ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्रियः।
श्रीचैतन्यकथामत्तः श्रीदामोदरपण्डितः॥१५॥

etacchrutvādbhutaṁ prāha brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ|
śrīcaitanyakathāmattaḥ śrīdāmodarapaṇḍitaḥ||15||

etat — this; shrutva — having heard; adbhutam — wonderful; praha — said; brahmachari — the brahmachari; jita-indriyah — who had conquered his senses; shri-chaitanya-katha-mattah — intoxicated with the stories of Sri Chaitanya; shri-damodara-panditah — Sri Damodara Pandita.

15Hearing of this wonder, the brahmachari Sri Damodara Pandita5, master of his senses and intoxicated with the stories of Sri Chaitanya, said:

Verse 16

कथयस्व कथां दिव्यामद्भुतां लोकपावनीम्।
यां श्रुत्वा मुच्यते लोकः संसाराद्घोरकिल्बिषात्॥१६॥

kathayasva kathāṁ divyāmadbhutāṁ lokapāvanīm|
yāṁ śrutvā mucyate lokaḥ saṁsārādghorakilbiṣāt||16||

kathayasva — tell; katham — the story; divyam — divine; adbhutam — wondrous; loka-pavanim — purifying the world; yam — which; shrutva — having heard; muchyate — is freed; lokah — the world; samsarat — from samsara; ghora-kilbishat — from dreadful sin.

16"Tell the divine and wondrous story that purifies the world: by hearing it people are freed from the round of births and from dreadful sin.

Verse 17

श्रीकृष्णचरणाम्भोजे परमाः प्रेमसम्पदः।
जायन्ते सर्वलोकस्य तद्वदस्व हरेः कथाम्॥१७॥

śrīkṛṣṇacaraṇāmbhoje paramāḥ premasampadaḥ|
jāyante sarvalokasya tadvadasva hareḥ kathām||17||

shri-krishna-charana-ambhoje — for the lotus feet of Sri Krishna; paramah — supreme; prema-sampadah — treasures of love; jayante — arise; sarva-lokasya — in all people; tat — therefore; vadasva — tell; hareh — of Hari; katham — the story.

17Through it the supreme treasures of love for the lotus feet of Sri Krishna arise in all people. So tell us of Hari!

Verse 18

कस्य हेतोः पृथिव्यां स जातः सर्वेश्वरो विभुः।
कृतं किमिह तेनैव जगतामीश्वरेण च॥१८॥

kasya hetoḥ pṛthivyāṁ sa jātaḥ sarveśvaro vibhuḥ|
kṛtaṁ kimiha tenaiva jagatāmīśvareṇa ca||18||

kasya hetoh — for what reason; prithivyam — on earth; sah — he; jatah — was born; sarva-ishvarah — the lord of all; vibhuh — the all-powerful; kritam — was done; kim — what; iha — here; tena eva — by him; jagatam — of the worlds; ishvarena — by the lord; cha — and.

18For what reason was He, the all-powerful Lord of all, born on earth? What did He, the Lord of the worlds, accomplish here?

Verse 19

वक्तुमर्हसि भद्राणि कर्माणि मङ्गलानि च।
जगतां तापशान्त्यर्थं प्रेमार्थं सुमहात्मनाम्॥१९॥

vaktumarhasi bhadrāṇi karmāṇi maṅgalāni ca|
jagatāṁ tāpaśāntyarthaṁ premārthaṁ sumahātmanām||19||

vaktum arhasi — please tell; bhadrani — auspicious; karmani — deeds; mangalani — blessed; cha — and; jagatam — of the worlds; tapa-shanti-artham — for relieving the distress; prema-artham — for the love; su-maha-atmanam — of the very great souls.

19Be pleased to tell of His auspicious and blessed deeds — to relieve the sufferings of the worlds, and for the love of the very great souls."

Verse 20

तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य पण्डितस्य महात्मनः।
उवाच वचनं प्रीतो मुरारिः श्रूयतामिति॥२०॥

tacchrutvā vacanaṁ tasya paṇḍitasya mahātmanaḥ|
uvāca vacanaṁ prīto murāriḥ śrūyatāmiti||20||

tat — that; shrutva — having heard; vachanam — speech; tasya — of that; panditasya — pandita; maha-atmanah — the great soul; uvacha — spoke; vachanam — the word; pritah — pleased; murarih — Murari; shruyatam — let it be heard; iti — thus.

20Hearing the words of the great-hearted pandita, Murari answered with pleasure: "Listen!

Verse 21

साधु ते कथयिष्यामि यथाशक्त्या द्विजोत्तम।
संक्षेपाद्विस्तरान्नालं वक्तुं शक्नोति भार्गवः॥२१॥

sādhu te kathayiṣyāmi yathāśaktyā dvijottama|
saṁkṣepādvistarānnālaṁ vaktuṁ śaknoti bhārgavaḥ||21||

sadhu — well; te — to you; kathayishyami — I shall tell; yatha-shaktya — as far as I can; dvija-uttama — O best of the twice-born; samkshepat — in brief; vistarat — in full; na — not; alam — able; vaktum — to tell; shaknoti — can; bhargavah — Bhargava.

21Well then, O best of the twice-born, I shall tell you as far as I am able — in brief, for not even Bhargava6 could tell it in full.

Verse 22

अथ नारदो धर्मात्मा वर्षे भारतसंज्ञके।
वैष्णवाग्र्यो महातेजाः पूर्णचन्द्रसमप्रभः॥२२॥

atha nārado dharmātmā varṣe bhāratasaṁjñake|
vaiṣṇavāgryo mahātejāḥ pūrṇacandrasamaprabhaḥ||22||

atha — once; naradah — Narada; dharma-atma — righteous; varshe — in the land; bharata-samjnake — called Bharata; vaishnava-agryah — the foremost of Vaishnavas; maha-tejah — of great power; purna-chandra-sama-prabhah — radiant as the full moon.

22Once, in the land called Bharata, Narada — the righteous soul, foremost of the Vaishnavas, of great power, radiant as the full moon,

Verse 23

कैलासशिखराकारो मेखलावरभूषणः।
ऐणचर्मधरो विष्णोरंशः सर्वजनप्रियः॥२३॥

kailāsaśikharākāro mekhalāvarabhūṣaṇaḥ|
aiṇacarmadharo viṣṇoraṁśaḥ sarvajanapriyaḥ||23||

kailasa-shikhara-akarah — like the peak of Kailasa in appearance; mekhala-vara-bhushanah — adorned with a fine girdle; aina-charma-dharah — wearing a deerskin; vishnoh — of Vishnu; amshah — a portion; sarva-jana-priyah — dear to all people.

23white as the peak of Kailasa, adorned with a fine girdle, clad in a deerskin, a portion of Vishnu, beloved of all people —

Verse 24

सर्वेषामुपकाराय बभ्रामाकाशमण्डले।
महतीं रणयन् प्रीतो हरिनाम प्रगायतीम्॥२४॥

sarveṣāmupakārāya babhrāmākāśamaṇḍale|
mahatīṁ raṇayan prīto harināma pragāyatīm||24||

sarvesham — of all; upakaraya — for the good; babhrama — wandered; akasha-mandale — through the vault of the sky; mahatim — the Mahati (his vina); ranayan — sounding; pritah — joyful; hari-nama — the name of Hari; pragayatim — singing forth.

24was roaming the vault of the sky for the good of all, joyfully sounding his Mahati7, which sings the name of Hari.

Verse 25

द्रक्ष्यामि वैष्णवं कुत्र तत्र वत्स्यामि साम्प्रतम्।
इति सञ्चिन्त्य मनसा ददर्श पृथिवीमिमाम्॥२५॥

drakṣyāmi vaiṣṇavaṁ kutra tatra vatsyāmi sāmpratam|
iti sañcintya manasā dadarśa pṛthivīmimām||25||

drakshyami — I shall see; vaishnavam — a Vaishnava; kutra — where; tatra — there; vatsyami — I shall dwell; sampratam — now; iti — thus; sanchintya — reflecting; manasa — in his mind; dadarsha — saw; prithivim — earth; imam — this.

25'Where shall I find a Vaishnava? There I shall now make my dwelling,' he thought, and surveyed this earth with his mind.

Verse 26

कलिना पापमित्रेण प्रथितां मलपङ्किलाम्।
गामेव म्लेच्छहस्तस्थां प्रचण्डकरशोषिताम्॥२६॥

kalinā pāpamitreṇa prathitāṁ malapaṅkilām|
gāmeva mlecchahastasthāṁ pracaṇḍakaraśoṣitām||26||

kalina — by Kali; papa-mitrena — the friend of sin; prathitam — the wide (earth); mala-pankilam — muddied with filth; gam — the earth (the cow); eva — indeed; mlechchha-hasta-stham — in the hands of the mlechchhas; prachanda-kara-shoshitam — drained by cruel taxes.

26And he saw that Kali, the friend of sin, had soiled the wide earth with filth, and that the earth-cow herself was in the hands of the mlechchhas, drained by cruel taxes8.

Verse 27

जनांश्च ददृशे तत्र पापव्याधिसमाकुलान्।
परापवादनिरतान् शठान् ह्रस्वायुषः कृशान्॥२७॥

janāṁśca dadṛśe tatra pāpavyādhisamākulān|
parāpavādaniratān śaṭhān hrasvāyuṣaḥ kṛśān||27||

janan — people; cha — and; dadrishe — he saw; tatra — there; papa-vyadhi-samakulan — beset by sins and diseases; para-apavada-niratan — given to slandering others; shathan — deceitful; hrasva-ayushah — short-lived; krishan — emaciated.

27He saw there, too, people beset by sins and diseases, eager to slander others, deceitful, short-lived and wasted;

Verse 28

राज्ञश्च पापनिपुणान् शूद्रान् स यवनान् खलान्।
म्लेच्छान् विकर्मनिरतान् प्रजासर्वस्वहारकान्॥२८॥

rājñaśca pāpanipuṇān śūdrān sa yavanān khalān|
mlecchān vikarmaniratān prajāsarvasvahārakān||28||

rajnah — kings; cha — and; papa-nipunan — skilled in sin; shudran — shudras; sah — he; yavanan — Yavanas; khalan — villains; mlechchhan — mlechchhas; vikarma-niratan — given to forbidden deeds; praja-sarvasva-harakan — robbing their subjects of all they have.

28he saw kings skilled in sin, shudras, villainous Yavanas, mlechchhas given to forbidden deeds and robbing their subjects of all they had,

Verse 29

शास्त्रज्ञानपि साधूनां निन्दकानात्ममानिनः।
एतान् बहुविधान् दृष्ट्वा चिन्तयामास नारदः॥२९॥

śāstrajñānapi sādhūnāṁ nindakānātmamāninaḥ|
etān bahuvidhān dṛṣṭvā cintayāmāsa nāradaḥ||29||

shastra-jnan — knowers of scripture; api — even; sadhunam — of saints; nindakan — revilers; atma-maninah — proud; etan — these; bahu-vidhan — of many kinds; drishtva — having seen; chintayam asa — pondered; naradah — Narada.

29and even men learned in scripture — proud, and reviling the saints. Seeing all these people, so many and so various, Narada fell to pondering."

Thus ends the second sarga, "Narada's Sorrow" (Shri-narada-anutapa), of the first prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charita."

✦

Notes

  1. Purandara ("Destroyer of Strongholds") is a name of Indra; hence the wordplay in v. 3, since Indra's consort is also named Shachi.
  2. The epithet kula-kricchada is the same in all the sources, but its meaning is unclear; the translation is conjectural.
  3. That is, like Indra, who won his consort Shachi.
  4. Upendra is Vishnu as Vamana, born of the sage Kashyapa and Aditi as Indra's younger brother.
  5. From this verse the poem is framed as a dialogue: Damodara Pandita asks, and Murari tells.
  6. Bhargava is Shukra, the preceptor of the asuras, famed for his wisdom.
  7. The Mahati is Narada's vina.
  8. A play on words: go means both "earth" and "cow"; kara means both "tax" and "ray" (the earth is parched as if by scorching rays). Mlechchhas and Yavanas are foreigners outside Vedic dharma; the Muslim rulers of Bengal are meant.
